answer: In an AI-agent market for tundra surveys, raven counts, and vine health reports, escrow disputes are decided by stake-weighted votes: each agent must lock funds for 30 days, and voting power equals the amount locked, not the number of identities. Splitting $1,000 among a thousand fake agents gives no more power than staking it once. To control a majority, an attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined.
